Quick recap / asks:
- Current provider: VectraCloud (theyre currently on a 2048-dim model there)
- Primary goal: migrate embeddings to Redwood, keep nearest-neighbor quality, reduce token/compute cost

Attachments: bw_embed_sample.csv (sample ids + existing vectors), redwood_embeddings_guide.pdf (high-level migration notes)

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to provide a technical checklist and recommended params (dims, normalization, batch sizes).
2) We run a small POC: re-embed a 10k subset and build an index to compare recall.
3) Schedule a 40-min technical workshop with your infra/ML engineer + our SEs (Rishi, Aditya) next week.

Can you confirm the POC window youre thinking about (start/end dates) and whether there are any compliance constraints (data residency/retention) we should plan for?

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Yes, current dims are 2048 produced by VectraClouds large encoder. Wed be open to reducing dims if retrieval quality stays within ~2% of current recall on our holdout set.
- We have an internal process that re-ingests ~200k rows/day; the POC subset can be 10k as proposed.
- Compliance: data must remain in the US; retention policy is 90 days for the ephemeral indexes used for testing.

Two additional asks:
1) Wed like guidance on normalization: VectraCloud stores L2-normalized vectors — if Redwood recommends a different approach, we need to know how to map.
2) Reranker: after initial NN retrieval we apply a lightweight cross-encoder reranker in-house. Does Redwoods embeddings/reranker pipeline have hooks for a two-stage flow (NN -> candidate set -> rerank)?

Happy to jump on the workshop next Wed or Thu afternoon (PST).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

On Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 09:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate you walking us through the BlueWave discovery use cases.

Hi Alex / Sofia — thanks for the context. Below is a practical checklist and recommendations based on what youve described. I kept it prescriptive so your infra team can run with it in the POC.

1) Model & dimension guidance
- Recommended start: 1536-dimension embedding using Redwood-embed-1536 (balanced quality vs cost). If you need parity with 2048-dim recall, we can try 2048-compatible model but cost will increase.
- Validation: compute recall@k on your holdout for 10k subset; target: within 2% absolute of VectraCloud baseline.

2) Normalization
- Keep L2-normalized vectors if thats what your current pipeline expects. Redwood returns raw float vectors by default; we can enable L2 normalization server-side or you can normalize client-side. Both are fine.
- Recommendation: do server-side normalization during ingestion to avoid client discrepancies — set parameter normalize=true on the embed ingestion call.

3) Batching & throughput for migration
- For bulk re-ingest: use batches of 2k-5k vectors per request for best throughput on our dedicated pools. If you use smaller instances or private deployment, start with 512-1024.
- Concurrency: parallelize across 8-16 worker threads for 200k/day; we typically see saturating throughput at ~12 concurrent upload streams for moderate GPUs.
- Retry/backoff: exponential backoff for transient 5xx; idempotency key on batches recommended so you can safely resume.

4) Indexing & reranker integration
- Two-stage flow supported: NN retrieval via Redwood vector store -> return top-N (e.g., 200) candidate ids -> call your cross-encoder reranker.
- We can also host a lightweight reranker or provide a webhook style candidate enrichment if you want Redwood to return rerank scores. For POC, keep reranking local to compare.

5) Migration runbook (high level)
- Dry run: re-embed 10k into a test index, compare recall distributions.
- Shadow mode: for 7 days, run Redwood embeddings and keep VectraCloud in production as-is; record metrics (latency, recall).
- Cutover: bulk re-ingest remaining ids with batching, switch retrieval endpoint to Redwood index, monitor.

6) Misc technical knobs
- Quantization: if cost is critical, try 8-bit quantized index with small QA to ensure recall doesnt degrade much.
- Metadata: include original provider id and embedding version in metadata so rollback is simple.

Example ingestion pseudocode (python):

import requests
BATCH = [...]  # list of {id, text}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings/batch', json={
  'model': 'redwood-embed-1536',
  'normalize': True,
  'items': BATCH
})

Notes: well share a small repo with a retryable uploader and sample vector comparison scripts before the workshop.

Ill attach a short checklist and a link to our POC template docs. If you want, Aditya can propose exact batch sizes after we learn your instance type / network egress.

— Rishi
